It was a historically tough year for Democrats – but together, we beat the odds and kept Colorado's seat blue by a 1.7% margin, the second closest that cycle. I continued working alongside him, supporting candidates, ballot measures, and legislation to invest in leveling the playing field for kids and regular people like me. Because, like he's always said: someone's ZIP code should never be the deciding factor in the opportunities they receive. As Michael prioritized our shared values at the federal level – most notably by nearly halving the national child poverty rate with the passage of the Child Tax Credit – he inspired me to lead the charge from here at home by running for Colorado's legislature. There, I worked to expand early childhood education, lower health care and medication costs, and create more opportunity for all Coloradans. And since 2023, I've had the honor of keeping up the fight for those values with Michael on the opposite side of Capitol Hill, as the U.S. representative for Colorado's 7th District. All of this is to say: Michael Bennet has been one of my most important mentors, role models, and allies from the very start. Dear USO Supporter,
During the government shutdown, many of our nation's service members will continue to stand guard and serve our country -- even as uncertainty looms at home -- and the USO is with them. Now is the time to show them that the appreciation of the USO and its supporters never stops either.
For military families already balancing the challenges of service, this moment can bring added stress and uncertainty. Past government shutdowns have lasted more than a month, and with many military families living paycheck to paycheck, this can have a significant impact on their lives.
At the USO, our mission is to be there for our nation's military 24/7, 365 days a year. We want to show our service members and their families our deepest gratitude -- but we cannot do it without your help.

clean_body: USO Supporter, stand with our military Dear USO Supporter, During the government shutdown, many of our nation's service members will continue to stand guard and serve our country -- even as uncertainty looms at home -- and the USO is with them. Now is the time to show them that the appreciation of the USO and its supporters never stops either. For military families already balancing the challenges of service, this moment can bring added stress and uncertainty. Past government shutdowns have lasted more than a month, and with many military families living paycheck to paycheck, this can have a significant impact on their lives. At the USO, our mission is to be there for our nation's military 24/7, 365 days a year. We want to show our service members and their families our deepest gratitude -- but we cannot do it without your help. Thank you for supporting our heroes in uniform today, tomorrow and always. | I’m running to serve you for four more years because our work to deliver on the Arizona Promise has only just begun. From cutting taxes for middle-class families, small businesses, and veterans, to lowering childcare costs, to erasing medical debt for over 350,000 Arizonans, I’m focused on creating real solutions for our state’s toughest challenges – unlike the Washington politicians who prefer to play partisan games. I’m proud to be the first social worker ever elected governor in this country. Arizonans don’t need out-of-touch, career politicians who care more about billionaires than working families – they deserve leaders who actually understand the struggles we face. I know what working families are going through — because I’ve lived it. I grew up in a working-class family in the heart of Tempe. I worked at Burger King and Pizza Hut to put myself through school. I lost my home in the Great Recession. I drove for Uber to make ends meet. My husband and I are still paying off student loans. _"Kentucky has regained $17.8 million in federal funding to build out electric vehicle charging stations following a successful challenge to a federal freeze on the money, Gov. Andy Beshear announced."_ Peter,

Gov. Andy Beshear is focused on moving Kentucky forward.

He just announced $17.8 million in federal funding to build out electric vehicle charging stations across the state — an investment that will create jobs, attract new businesses, and ensure Kentucky families are part of a growing new economic sector.

Andy has made it clear that when Washington makes Kentucky a promise, he'll do everything he can to make sure our people get what they're owed. This is what good leadership looks like, Peter: Focusing on the things that make life better for the people you serve.

He isn’t playing partisan games or chasing headlines; he's delivering real results that will strengthen communities and prepare us for the future. That's why we need to have his back. While Andy is working to grow our economy and protect Kentucky families, he's also fighting tooth and nail to elect more for-the-people leaders across the nation who will always put Americans FIRST.

**I’m running to serve you for four more years because our work to deliver on the Arizona Promise has only just begun. From cutting taxes for middle-class families, small businesses, and veterans, to lowering childcare costs, to erasing medical debt for over 350,000 Arizonans, I’m focused on creating real solutions for our state’s toughest challenges — unlike the Washington politicians who prefer to play partisan games.**
I’m proud to be the first social worker ever elected governor in this country. Arizonans don’t need out-of-touch, career politicians who care more about billionaires than working families – they deserve leaders who actually understand the struggles we face.
I know what working families are going through — because I’ve lived it. I grew up in a working-class family in the heart of Tempe. I worked at Burger King and Pizza Hut to put myself through school. I lost my home in the Great Recession. I drove for Uber to make ends meet. My husband and I are still paying off student loans.

**It all began with Trump ordering a map redraw in Texas to help the GOP pick up five House seats.**
The extreme racial gerrymander was signed into law despite Republicans already holding 25 of the 38 congressional seats in Texas.
Missouri’s governor signed a new map into law that will give the GOP an additional seat. If upheld, Republicans will hold seven of the state’s eight congressional districts.
Utah Republicans advanced a map that would shore up control of _all_ of the state’s congressional seats — despite a district court ruling that struck down the state’s gerrymandered map.
Now, Indiana, Louisiana, Ohio, Florida, Nebraska, and Kansas are all considering new maps before the midterm elections to give Trump his wish to ensure victory in the midterms, _despite_ how Americans vote.
**This is a nationwide threat to fair representation.**
[**The NDRC and the fair maps movement are fighting back on all fronts — and in all these states — using every tool in our toolbox. But we need strong grassroots support to keep up this critical work. Hi, it's Mikie Sherrill, Democratic Nominee for NJ Governor.
I’ve told you time and time again just how important this race is for New Jersey.
But what you need to understand is, what we do here will have major implications for the country.
This is the first major election since Donald Trump returned to office. Since then, we’ve seen nothing but chaos and corruption come from the White House — and New Jersey families have taken hit after hit because of it.
On November 4, New Jerseyans have an important choice to make: we can choose the career politician who’s going to copy and paste Trump’s disastrous policies into New Jersey, or we can choose a new way forward: a leader who will always put our state first, and never bend to the will of deep-pocketed Washington politicians.
And if we win, not only do we send a powerful message to the nation by choosing the path of affordability, opportunity, and freedom — we empower Democrats across the country to stand up and fight back against the Trump administration, setting us up for major wins in 2026, 2028, and beyond.
Whatever happens, America is going to follow New Jersey’s lead. That’s why National Republicans are pouring millions of dollars into this race, it’s why Donald Trump and his administration have attacked me repeatedly, and it’s why we have to win this election.
The movement we’re building here in New Jersey is so much bigger than me or you — it’s about all of us coming together to build a new path forward for our state, and for our country. And if that’s the type of movement you believe in, I would really appreciate it if you split whatever you can between my team and Tobias Read to help power me to victory this Election Day. name: Kirk Cameron
subject: The left is creating a generation of confused and fearful children
body:
If you haven't heard about the "See You at the Library Day" on Fox News or Newsmax or your other favorite news sources, please let me tell you why it's so critical.

| | |
---
| | Fellow conservative, I know you've seen how the Left is creating a generation of fearful and confused children. And boy, the ALA and radical librarians didn't like that one bit. >> Over 50 libraries rejected our request to host our Story Hour. >> The ALA helped local libraries scheme ways to keep us out including booking all the event rooms for themselves. >> Social media blew up with attacks: I was compared to a Nazi (that's original), BRAVE Books was accused of trying to "confuse and demoralize children," our supporters were described as "bored moms/busybodies who need something to feel good about," and on and on. I can't even print most things these radicals said because it's so vile. In the end we got two libraries to reverse course by reminding them that their censorship violated the Constitution of the United States. And thousands of parents and grandparents brought their little ones to those Story Hours where we pledged allegiance to the flag, sang "God Bless America," and read wholesome and Godly books. It was incredible. But here's the greatest part... From there, parents and grandparents started asking BRAVE Books how they could host Story Hours of their own. So BRAVE Books has organized a nationwide grassroots "See You at the Library" movement to take back our libraries. Now with the guidance of BRAVE Books , committed conservatives just like you book event rooms at their local library for conservative Story Hours that fill children's hearts with goodness, gratitude, and God. And whenever we can, BRAVE Books authors like swimmer Riley Gaines , TV personality Missy Robertson , and myself stand shoulder-to-shoulder with conservative parents, grandparents, and patriots at these Story Hours... ...for a very simple mission - to reject the Left's radical ideas and reclaim childhood innocence in America's libraries. 2025 was the third year of "See You at the Library" and I'm proud to say that because of the amazing support of patriots like you, we were invited by President Trump's DOE to kick off our event at the Library of Congress! What a testimony it was to bring our message of freedom, America's greatness, and God's love to children and families in the heart of our nation's capital. Now we have a new and historic goal for 2026 - the 250th birthday of our nation! We aim to reach 250,000 children in the next year. But we can't do it without you. Your sponsorship gift will be used to send a "Story Hour Kit" to every parent, grandparent, and patriot who's organizing an event at their library. The kit includes everything they need to bring your conservative values back into our public libraries: instructions for booking their library space and running their Story Hour, small American flags for the little ones, fun stickers, wholesome books, Bible memory verse cards, and other specialty items. BRAVE Books is a small Christian company. They don't have the millions behind them like the giant taxpayer-funded ALA. Your sponsorship gift is the only way we can fund our Story Hours for over 250,000 children to counter the radical leftists who've taken control of our libraries. Knowing that, That's enough to sponsor one entire "Story Hour Kit" yourself. Singlehandedly, you'll be reaching 50 children with our wholesome, Godly, and patriotic message. Thank you! [](https://act.gallegoforarizona.com/go/1000?c0=ruben-hobbs-em-split.OtSY65&refcode=em251009-1-90&t=27&akid=4013%2E734936%2EVHxtL8)
I grew up in a working-class family in the heart of Tempe. When my dad was between jobs, my family relied on our church community and food stamps to get by.
I got my first job at 16, working at Burger King and then Pizza Hut to put myself through high school and college. My husband and I raised our kids through the Great Recession, experienced a home foreclosure, and we’re still paying off our student loans.
Even after I was elected to public office, I took a second job driving for Uber to make sure my kids had Christmas presents.
So when I say this work is personal to me, I mean it. I know deeply what it’s like to do whatever it takes to provide for your family.
**As governor, I’ve always pledged to fight just as hard every day for your family as I fought for mine – and that’s what I promise to keep doing when re-elected.**
Over the last three years, we’ve cut taxes for middle-class families, small businesses, and veterans. We lowered childcare costs so working parents aren’t saddled with yet another expense. We erased medical debt for more than 350,000 Arizonans.
**_But all our progress is on the line in this race._**

clean_body: We are the leaders we’ve been waiting for. | | | Peter, the word is out! 🤭 We're bringing together United We Dream’s founders, past members, and current leaders at our first Congress in nearly a decade — and ! In a year where our communities have faced deep uncertainty, we need space to reconnect with our roots, recharge, and reflect on the important roles we each play in shaping our future. We, the people, have the power. Our 2025 Digital Congress is the opportunity to be in community once again with immigrant youth and allies who care about building a future where we can all thrive. 👉 Join us on Sunday, November 9, at 12:30 pm CT/1:30 pm ET for our 2025 Digital Congress:Uniting in the Face of Adversity!** When you attend our Digital Congress, you’ll: 🤝 Connect with immigrants, working people, students, and educators who are committed to working together to deliver the future our communities need 📍Hear from UWD members about the work they are doing in their communities, and learn how you can take action locally! 🧡 Receive a FREE sticker to be reminded of your spirit of resilience and our vision for an abundant future for all, wherever you go Throughout the years, Congress has been a place where young people can feel empowered to come out as undocumented and unafraid, and learn from one another about the ways we’re each bringing our communities into action. This year, our Digital Congress meets you where you are, offering a safe space to build community and discover the role you can play in this movement! 🗓️ See you there, Ximena and the UWD team P.S.: Forward this invitation to your friends today! 📨 | Follow us on: | | | | |

body:
Defend Our Courts has been blaring the alarm for months, and now PA Governor Josh Shapiro is entering the fray and getting involved in this fight.
| | |
---
| | [](https://wep8ryhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001JIuxRVPLSDVRoBiSILI8oHNJcUnKu6X0-Ux1x0PRNE7nK6O-z3t5AWcddFgWUCWZ6klgpi_Tr7vkAESgkf-NO_LIvs8F-BSCMGv0_BwO-iMoBkcdABV0gNGx8ISHnxA8QrUI9Ixjk3qqGHfNOpX-mq1b-5sxI8XLH9mnizSXreMFkya3oktATa9NaRnWpo_Y4MveghRnso-4dECxZM-MPj2A5cviTKLw05NqBgcchu4=&c=qGAP-jiyqUIxTuYczs3m4ha7a76XS4HWitqi8ht-ODLTVFl1aVao8A==&ch=7nlAqCDF_hzEldyMmdpQB7uv8ZP2AdDtCL_OEARXz7tljXNp9_IoEA==)

| Friend,
One animating principle our team at Defend Our Courts adopted from the start of this battle to save three Democratic justices on the Pennsylvania Supreme Court is this: "Be bold and mighty forces will come to your aid."
But heading into this critical contest, barely any Democrats knew there was even an election happening in PA this November. Even fewer were aware of what was at risk if we lost.
All the while, MAGA activists had been working around the clock behind the scenes registering new Republican voters and quietly plotting their strategy to trick voters in PA into tossing out all three Democratic judges in one fell swoop.
It would be nothing short of a devastating GOP coup if they pulled it off.

**When you first hear Kaizen Asiedu speak, you know immediately -- this is someone who refuses to take shortcuts with truth.**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/7f569354-a6a4-4d91-872d-96506cfa26b8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

A Harvard graduate with a degree in philosophy, Emmy Award winner, and cultural commentator with more than 800,000 followers, Kaizen has become one of the most trusted voices for Americans who feel politically homeless in today's polarized landscape.
Publicly endorsed by **Elon Musk** as a "clear thinker," Kaizen walked away from an Emmy-winning career in entertainment to pursue something far rarer -- **intellectual honesty**. Through his platform, **Clear Thinker Academy** , he teaches millions to cut through media bias and political manipulation using principles grounded in philosophy and peer-reviewed psychology.
> "My mission," Kaizen says, "is to restore clarity, nuance, and civil discourse to American culture -- to help people think independently and resist tribal groupthink, regardless of political affiliation."
We're honored to welcome **Kaizen Asiedu** as a featured speaker at the **Seed & Roots Summit 2025** -- _Faith. Family. And the Future of Work in America._
🗓 **Saturday, October 25, 2025**
📍 _Philadelphia, PA_ | _Independence Visitor Center_
⏰ _9:00 AM - 5:00 PM (Doors open at 8:30am)_
* * *
**Why this matters:**
In an age where outrage drowns out reflection, Kaizen is proving that clarity isn't weakness -- it's leadership.
Attached below is our official full speaker promo.

- Team Cori
Hi Peter,
What. A. Week.
In case you missed it, Cori Bush officially launched her campaign last Friday to represent Missouri’s First District again — and the momentum is already building.
Here’s what we’ve accomplished together in just a few days:
💜 Cori’s campaign launch video spread across St. Louis and beyond as thousands of supporters shared her message of courage, resilience, and love. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/upl_cab_email-launchvideo?refcode=x_251010_launchweekrecap_act]

WATCH CORI'S LAUNCH VIDEO [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/upl_cab_email-launchvideo?refcode=x_251010_launchweekrecap_act]
💜 Our website is officially live — laying out Cori’s vision for Missouri’s First District and giving supporters one place to learn, get involved, and take action. Check out our website here [https://www.coribush.org/] .
💜And now, endorsements are rolling in, and the people are showing up for her once again.
In just a few hours after announcing, Cori has already received the proud endorsements of key grassroots organizations like Our Revolution [https://www.instagram.com/p/DPW08kzDvAs/?hl=en] and Politivist Action PAC [https://www.instagram.com/p/DPWLj0NjO7f/?hl=en&img_index=1] . We look forward to growing this momentum as time goes on.
💜 And Peter, the media is paying attention.
Cori joined St. Louis Public Radio’s Politically Speaking podcast for an in-depth conversation about her record and her vision for St. Louis. [LISTEN HERE] [https://www.stlpr.org/podcast/politically-speaking/2025-10-04/missouri-congress-cori-bush-st-louis-fighter]
And she appeared on MSNBC’s Velshi for her first national interview of the campaign, reminding the country what true people-powered leadership looks like.

WATCH THE FULL INTERVIEW [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/upl_cab_email-msnbcvideo?refcode=x_251010_launchweekrecap_act]
💜 The people are showing up. Supporters like you have already helped us reach our launch fundraising goal! Real grassroots power is fueling this campaign every step of the way.
But let’s be real: the same corporate-backed interests who tried to unseat Cori last time are already lining up again. We can’t slow down now.
If you believe in Cori’s vision for a St. Louis that works for everyone, we need you with us.
Can you chip in today to fuel Cori’s comeback and keep St. Louis in the hands of the people? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/upl_cab_email-launchvideo?refcode=x_251010_launchweekrecap_act]
DONATE TODAY [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/upl_cab_email-launchvideo?refcode=x_251010_launchweekrecap_act]
St. Louis, we are just getting started. This is only the beginning.
With gratitude, love, and appreciation,
Team Cori

As a Congresswoman, she has always shown up when it’s hardest: securing disaster relief, lowering insulin costs, and delivering millions for our communities.
Across St. Louis, families are being priced out and pushed out. Cori Bush is fighting back for affordable housing, fair wages, and utilities as a human right. Be part of this people-first movement. Join Team Cori today and sign up to volunteer. [https://www.coribush.org]

Peter,

In the middle of a government shutdown that's already hurting families across Washington, Donald Trump just made things worse for folks across our district and state.

He canceled $1 billion in promised funding for the Pacific Northwest Hydrogen Hub— _one of the largest clean energy projects in the country that was set to power our region's economy for decades._

This wasn't just another federal program, it was a bipartisan priority that both Republicans and Democrats in the Northwest worked together to secure in order to make our region a national leader in clean hydrogen energy. But now, **thanks to Trump's petty politics, Washington State is losing out on:**
* $1 billion total investment
* $5 million in private investment
* $4 million for worker training
* 10,000 good-paying jobs across Washington and the Pacific Northwest
* A cleaner, more reliable energy future—including hydrogen power for aviation, trucking, and manufacturing

Peter, at a time when we need more clean energy than ever before, the president is working over time to strip Washington State of jobs, investment, and opportunity.

He's taking away our region's leadership in the world's energy future, and frankly, **he's doing it in a way that feels like retaliation against blue states.** But let's make one thing clear: This was a bipartisan effort because both Republicans and Democrats understood the positive impact it would have for Washingtonians—and Trump still went ahead with canceling this vital funding. That's NOT real leadership. It's plain wrong.

[**We can't let him get away with it, at least not without a fight. clean_body: Washington deserves better than political punishment. Peter, In the middle of a government shutdown that's already hurting families across Washington, Donald Trump just made things worse for folks across our district and state. He canceled $1 billion in promised funding for the Pacific Northwest Hydrogen Hub— one of the largest clean energy projects in the country that was set to power our region's economy for decades. This wasn't just another federal program, it was a bipartisan priority that both Republicans and Democrats in the Northwest worked together to secure in order to make our region a national leader in clean hydrogen energy. But now, thanks to Trump's petty politics, Washington State is losing out on: $1 billion total investment $5 million in private investment $4 million for worker training 10,000 good-paying jobs across Washington and the Pacific Northwest A cleaner, more reliable energy future—including hydrogen power for aviation, trucking, and manufacturing Peter, at a time when we need more clean energy than ever before, the president is working over time to strip Washington State of jobs, investment, and opportunity. He's taking away our region's leadership in the world's energy future, and frankly, he's doing it in a way that feels like retaliation against blue states. But let's make one thing clear: This was a bipartisan effort because both Republicans and Democrats understood the positive impact it would have for Washingtonians—and Trump still went ahead with canceling this vital funding. That's NOT real leadership. It's plain wrong. Thank you, Team Schrier Rep. Kim Schrier is a doctor, scientist, and mom, fighting for Washington's 8th District in Congress. body:
Here's what's happening in the Forward world...

| | [ ](https://home.forwardparty.com/r?u=JgyyvCfQwldlSeD7KJl_Ih7269o_4hwqOhPs1_PHvgI&e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=fast_forward_81a&n=1)

Thursday, October 09, 2025 | Peter -- Forward is Fighting for the Voice of Voters! The [_Polelle v. Florida_](https://home.forwardparty.com/r?u=TUOX35N7pYkptd7_GoTk5kmbNOTH9WE5SO3UYIou5TfFyoznKN470R0YcYCizsSD2hUH67g6VCPisvU6TpcLCeS8LAgPxBxTuCOM6tkpxRUNNpglVtRd2tR5rftxekqaszsDyhFm02SbVmQqf90sdK72ad0J0geJXGM_xH9rwiSknwstQrerhkI_htbo9057&e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=fast_forward_81a&n=2) case before the Supreme Court challenges whether states can bar independents from voting in primaries unless they register with a major party. The Forward Party is proud to stand alongside the Florida Forward Party, Open Primaries, the Independent Voter Project, and so many others in supporting the petition with this [amicus brief](https://home.forwardparty.com/r?u=YTIBxqx8zpmyL-AnxGUXEubKGXLUGN8HhNcBv97nZKSncQ9cpPamxwzQsy_snH3U8rXduIyA6Xihcq3O95F2dMiGT40uciudase1SMAQDrv7A7juTimWAFzpexBCvLWh&e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=fast_forward_81a&n=3) because it goes to the heart of what Forward stands for: fair representation and a voice for every voter. The Forward Party is fighting for a system where the rules are fair, leaders answer to all their voters (not just party insiders), and primaries don’t reward the extremes. Partisan gerrymandering and closed primaries are two of the main tools the major parties use to protect their turf. By drawing districts to lock in safe seats and shutting independents out of primaries, they silence the majority of U.S. voters and tighten their grip on power. The Supreme Court’s decision in _Polelle v. Florida_ could reshape the rules of our democracy and determine whether millions of independents are allowed full participation in elections. For the 40% of Americans who identify as independents, the stakes are huge. In Florida, where many districts are effectively decided in primaries, this exclusion forces voters to affiliate or be shut out of the process entirely. Closed primaries turn millions of citizens into second-class participants in elections they fund, silencing voices outside the duopoly. We exist to fix what’s broken in our politics, including closed primaries and partisan gerrymandering. Our candidates pledge to fight to strengthen democracy and elevate the voters’ voice. Make no mistake \- no matter how it couches the decision, the Supreme Court is deciding whether you get a say in your elected officials. With gerrymandering and closed primaries, it's party leadership who currently gets to decide on our representatives.
**[Maps shouldn't pick winners. Voters should. ](https://home.forwardparty.com/r?u=_KeSraPW0gSlxEBMOvJrEouH4SjeZmYtvTWulgNFAfYF8zdXyPEKnNSaGb3G_WW0&e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=fast_forward_81a&n=4)| Fox 5** Forward Party Communications Director John Goodwin joins FOX5 to break down how gerrymandering in Texas and California warps representation and why independent redistricting commissions lead to fairer maps that put voters first. [**Forward Party's Andrew Yang joins Bloomberg TV**](https://home.forwardparty.com/r?u=H5_jbWXkmQ8af757LskXhVZMb4_mamZ7BomvzN4HdKAqxiR-DbqNeZ5XURxu9xBG-31AtGazTdnAlsG_w6OvlfP4jPBKtQ1APF4rcs3Um75DSSZvgVFq9Y_4FmcHRNgvJFcMMpjKv3vl3I2rxIPEhA&e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=fast_forward_81a&n=5)**|****Bloomberg** Andrew Yang discusses the opportunities for third parties, the New York City mayoral race, and the federal government shutdown.
**October 14 | Women's Committee Strategy Session w/ FWD Political Director Kayla Berube** For our highly anticipated October meeting, we are thrilled to host Kayla Berube, Forward Party Political Director. Kayla will offer invaluable insights into current trends and progress in the political direction of the FWD Party for this general election plus 2026. For more information and to RSVP, click [here](https://home.forwardparty.com/women_s_committee_october_general_meeting?e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=fast_forward_81a&n=6). **October 16 | Cafecito Series: Conversations with FWD Hispanic & Latino Leaders** Join the Hispanic & Latino Committee & Young Forwardists for an engaging conversation with Forward Party endorsed candidates as they share their journeys into public service and the impact they hope to make in their communities. This event highlights the leadership, priorities, and innovative solutions these candidates bring to local challenges. Attendees will have the opportunity to hear directly from candidates committed to building stronger communities and driving meaningful change. For more information and to RSVP, click [here](https://home.forwardparty.com/hlc_candidate_forum_october_2025?e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=fast_forward_81a&n=7). **October 16 | The Forward Party – A Case Professorship Conversation (In Person Only)** Rutgers University Eagleton Institute of Politics hosts founders and leaders of The Forward Party—including Kerry Healey, Christine Todd Whitman, and Andrew Yang—in discussion of their public service careers, democratic values, and efforts to reimagine political discourse through a bipartisan lens. Click [here](https://home.forwardparty.com/r?u=p1Q1RNsNMLek2CLAHrySfp0fOjGCgdPQagDFOOemHm4s7bW-ot0hQNpSxnQ6fo_L6FGr16nI_hPFx6cTXgzxEOI1H8_KoefK0-W1ZTBGqZhJWVUUOzFSlT7QLUBc_js1&e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=fast_forward_81a&n=8) for more information. **October 17 | Open Primaries Primary Buzz Virtual Discussion** Open Primaries President John Opdycke will bring together some of the attorneys leading the charge and building a litigation platform and strategy for the reform movement. They’ll discuss the role of litigation in changing politics and how getting into court could transform the primary reform movement. Special guest, Michael Polelle, the initiator of the Florida lawsuit. Register [here](https://home.forwardparty.com/r?u=1bglchNhV5n7qaCqsDLY9R9iQmUTkU4fqZOl-Ju-qOc-oUlr24veyVfBIHjIOVICtrP2GkUiettC1KfcN5wb5gNK9h3JM0sjeMTUSxT3AFM&e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=fast_forward_81a&n=9).
[**Republicans could draw 19 more House seats after an upcoming Surpeme Court Ruling**](https://home.forwardparty.com/r?u=wWw1LGKe09YoyrHaTkDQ4GG1qh98GYcXj0zaOWKzAERGsDVkGTey0mlYoLj9uAfhMRaHq6SH9AIUDJ14OBu511JionFRA_zHr1DBUue_HRE&e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=fast_forward_81a&n=10) | **Politico** A new CNN poll takes a deeper look into who political independents are finds the notion of a classic swing voter is a thing of the past.

name: Derek Tran
subject: I’m fighting for our troops to be paid during the GOP shutdown.
body:
|
# [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/116946204/574955924/-1516755731?refcode=em-header&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDg3ODciLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiNDkzMzEwZWQtNTJhNS1mMDExLThlNjEtNjA0NWJkZWQ4YmE0IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=ZeogV3DowcjTHcmK3XZBD2_OsotDaGpZOo85Mv6lg7Y=)
Here’s something Republicans don’t want you to know about their shutdown:

**If Congress doesn’t act by October 15th, nearly __three million__ military families will go without a paycheck.**

I served in the Army. I know that every dollar in those paychecks makes a difference. With skyrocketing costs, losing out on just one paycheck can be disastrous.

It’s unacceptable that our troops would miss out on deserved pay because Washington can’t get its act together.

**That’s why I led my Democratic colleagues in calling on Speaker Mike Johnson to bring Congress back into session so we can ensure our service members and military contractors continue to get paid during the shutdown.**
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/116946207/574955939/-1516755731?refcode=em-10.9.25-all-b&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDg3ODciLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiNDkzMzEwZWQtNTJhNS1mMDExLThlNjEtNjA0NWJkZWQ4YmE0IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=ZeogV3DowcjTHcmK3XZBD2_OsotDaGpZOo85Mv6lg7Y=)

Voter Action Project [https://voteractionproject.org/]
Folks,
On September 25, 2025, the President released National Security Presidential Memorandum-7 (NSPM-7), titled “ Countering Domestic Terrorism and Organized Political Violence .” This memo contains broad and vague language that could allow government agencies to monitor or penalize individuals and groups based on their beliefs rather than their actions.
Terms like “anti-American,” “anti-capitalist,” and “anti-Christian” are so loosely defined that peaceful advocacy organizations, religious communities, or critics of government policy could be subject to investigation—even if they have no connection to violence of any kind. In our current political environment, it means partisan finger-pointing and extremism can be elevated from a difference of opinion to political retribution and punishment with no due process.
This raises serious constitutional questions about freedom of speech, religion, and association. It is essential that elected officials provide oversight before this policy is implemented further.
Call on Congress today to let them know that our right to free speech must be protected no matter who is in control of our government >> [https://actionnetwork.org/letters/a-new-federal-memo-could-silence-dissent-tell-congress-to-act?source=direct_link&referrer=group-integrity-first-voter-action-project&redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fsecure.actblue.com%2Fdonate%2Fifvap-actions]

body:
The Department of Justice should be pursuing accountability, cracking down on corruption, and defending the Constitution. But under this administration, the DOJ is a tool for attacking enemies and covering up wrongdoing. | | | |
---
Team —
Attorney General Pam Bondi appeared at her first oversight hearing after nine months of her stewardship of the Justice Department.
It was urgent — after all, hundreds of career prosecutors have quit because of the politicization of the Justice Department and the fear that they might have to take unethical actions at the direction of Trump and Bondi.
We’ve seen the DOJ cover up the corruption of the administration and its friends — like the WH Border Czar taking $50,000 in cash from undercover FBI agents. Or the corruption case against the Mayor of NYC. Or the Epstein files.
And we’ve seen the department prosecute the president’s enemies at the president’s urging — like James Comey — even though career prosecutors said the case lacked evidence.
Friend, it’s safe to say Pam Bondi was not too pleased with my line of questioning. Don’t just take it from me, look at some of the headlines from the hearing:
[ ](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqu_hjK98iroObSdPglX9oSTsp6wrz3hMvfKE7NxvZvhefU3U0BUQyKRzVCpkwzDKtuJ5jADkCh-CPlJN1GoRRMyYNAMmIyYFVUemyP6fcnGEBYWklzkQToJQwlMSkLgGoHtsN-C9FjgT98xHgsU6WVJjG9krEidAz3mDCvfexAY6kBWpIz7fIsZCiL17NqOylkJQJxCa_B8TVbmtipWmHq71HPSN5vG4Uj3U9v4fTAGB9kP-lnWuRcKeN-cd-BCY_eYadxblyDfyj511kpLdDT4Wd8Bi1Lapl_RzI6s-vIBszneQO4bkOytICSigGcgdRBKcN_PX08Cz-GXF4NrOHhyXThE_1X0pg2xyIr1Y1NgxWi0KLRjk7AKoteER31b2DACCKrh1ncYiVzyhlcf6lpZ/4kl/FpDU_9TIRni55QpbF_WOjw/h0/h001.ar8cDmeq3cS0p7Al5_V4RHrUldjqnBuWFCsknhGBqYc)
---
Friend, the Department of Justice has become Trump’s personal sword to go after his ever-growing list of political enemies, including me. And his shield to cover up corruption and hide wrongdoing.
And Pam Bondi has enabled this behavior.
Instead of going after Tom Homan, Trump’s border czar, for taking the 50 thousand in cash, the DOJ shut down the investigation.
When I asked Attorney General Bondi about this, she deflected responsibility. Said she didn’t know or wouldn’t comment about the case. She said that I should be **fired**. _Team, she even said I should apologize to Donald Trump for leading his first impeachment trial._
_Not gonna happen._
The Department of Justice should be pursuing accountability, cracking down on corruption, and defending the Constitution. But under this administration, the DOJ is a tool for attacking enemies and covering up wrongdoing.
I will continue to use my position on the Judiciary Committee to conduct hard oversight and demand concrete answers. I will call out corruption and speak out against any and every attempt to weaponize our legal system against Trump’s political opponents. I will not give in, and not back down.

clean_body: The Department of Justice should be pursuing accountability, cracking down on corruption, and defending the Constitution. But under this administration, the DOJ is a tool for attacking enemies and covering up wrongdoing. | | | | Team — Attorney General Pam Bondi appeared at her first oversight hearing after nine months of her stewardship of the Justice Department. It was urgent — after all, hundreds of career prosecutors have quit because of the politicization of the Justice Department and the fear that they might have to take unethical actions at the direction of Trump and Bondi. We’ve seen the DOJ cover up the corruption of the administration and its friends — like the WH Border Czar taking $50,000 in cash from undercover FBI agents. Or the corruption case against the Mayor of NYC. Or the Epstein files. And we’ve seen the department prosecute the president’s enemies at the president’s urging — like James Comey — even though career prosecutors said the case lacked evidence. Friend, it’s safe to say Pam Bondi was not too pleased with my line of questioning. Don’t just take it from me, look at some of the headlines from the hearing: Friend, the Department of Justice has become Trump’s personal sword to go after his ever-growing list of political enemies, including me. And his shield to cover up corruption and hide wrongdoing. And Pam Bondi has enabled this behavior. Instead of going after Tom Homan, Trump’s border czar, for taking the 50 thousand in cash, the DOJ shut down the investigation. When I asked Attorney General Bondi about this, she deflected responsibility. Said she didn’t know or wouldn’t comment about the case. She said that I should be fired. Team, she even said I should apologize to Donald Trump for leading his first impeachment trial. Not gonna happen. The Department of Justice should be pursuing accountability, cracking down on corruption, and defending the Constitution. But under this administration, the DOJ is a tool for attacking enemies and covering up wrongdoing. I will continue to use my position on the Judiciary Committee to conduct hard oversight and demand concrete answers. I will call out corruption and speak out against any and every attempt to weaponize our legal system against Trump’s political opponents. I will not give in, and not back down. Dear Peter, I’d like to have an honest conversation with you about our great state. I believe our future is bright and Alaska’s best days are ahead of us. **That’s why today, I’m excited to officially launch my campaign to be our next governor.** As lieutenant governor, I’ve fought tough battles for Alaskans. As Commissioner of Corrections, I fought to repeal soft-on-crime laws _and won_. And in the state legislature, I went up against politicians in Juneau to protect the PFD _and won_. I promise to bring the same grit and common sense to the Governor’s office, because I want to ensure Alaska remains the best place to live, work, and raise a family for our kids and grandkids. # [](https://act.adamschiff.com/go/61?t=1&akid=9062%2E5257348%2EYeSeAZ)
Derek —
We’re nine days into the government shutdown.
You might be wondering: _How is the president using his time to try to bring an end to the pain he is inflicting on the American people?_
→ He’s spent time addressing hundreds of generals and admirals, telling them that they need to train in American cities and consider the American people in those cities as “the enemy within.”
→ He ordered a strike on another ship in the Caribbean — an action he did not have the authority to conduct.
→ He’s gone after American universities, in an effort to coerce these schools into following his agenda — or else, they’ll lose federal dollars.
→ He’s methodically punishing his enemies — threatening again to lay off thousands of people and cut billions in funding for vital programs. **His focus is on money and programs in Blue states that didn’t vote for him.**
→ He’s cancelling energy projects in California, which will directly drive up energy prices.
→ He's using _your_ tax dollars to push out propaganda on government websites and using the emails of government employees without their permission.
→ He’s been trolling and posting on social media.
→ And of course, he’s been out on the golf course.
Normally, presidents try to minimize the harm of a government shutdown. They try to bring together the parties in Congress and end the shutdown.
**But not Donald Trump. No, he is trying to maximize the harm — but only in certain parts of the country.**
This kind of petty, vindictive politics is not new. But that doesn’t mean we have to accept this behavior as normal.
Meanwhile, Republicans are starting to panic, aware of the fact that millions of Americans are about to get giant increases to their health care insurance — and the public is going to be pissed. They have every right to be. This is entirely a crisis engineered entirely by Republicans to pay for their tax cuts for rich people.
We need to speak out, demand Republicans come to the table, address this health care crisis, and end this shutdown.
More soon from me,
Adam

We’ve been fighting this lonely battle all year. First, warning that these deployments were coming. Then, preparing elected leaders in states at highest risk of Trump’s wrath. And now, raising hell against them.
It’s having an impact — and now is not the time to let up.

name: JB Pritzker
subject: Jon Ossoff
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Jon Ossoff for SenateThis email was sent to dpwillis67@gmail
body:
Jon Ossoff is the GOP’s #1 target and he needs our help:
#

[
---
Peter, it’s JB Pritzker. In a minute, I’m going to ask you to [**join me in supporting Jon Ossoff by chipping in to his reelection campaign.**](https://act.electjon.com/go/32?c0=ossoff-em-oct25.ZBiurg&refcode=em251009-1-f-sb&t=2&akid=895%2E5691347%2ErmjpPS) But first, I hope you’ll let me explain why Georgia’s Senate race will be one of the most important elections on the map in 2026: _We aren’t even a year into Trump’s second term, and he’s already forcing his unpopular and harmful agenda on the American people._ He’s stripping folks of their health care, cutting veterans’ services, and threatening to revoke citizenship from American citizens — all while he makes unprecedented grabs for power and attempts to establish himself as an authoritarian strongman. Look, it’s clear that as Trump’s madman tendencies grip the nation and harm working families, we need leaders everywhere to step up and fight back to protect our democracy. **Jon Ossoff has proven himself to be one of those leaders, Peter.** Before being elected by the people of Georgia, Jon led a team of investigative journalists that uncovered human rights abuses and unjust practices by corrupt governments. He’s brought that knowledge to the Senate where he’s acted as a watchdog for the Trump administration’s unconstitutional overreach on our government. We cannot lose Jon Ossoff’s leadership in the Senate. But Republicans have made him their top target in 2026, meaning this will likely be the most competitive and expensive election in the country. Jon can defend his seat and continue his important work in Washington — but he needs folks to step up and help him win this race. [**Peter, will you join me in supporting Jon Ossoff’s reelection campaign by pitching in any amount today? Whether it’s $5, $10, or whatever you’re able to give, it’ll go a long way in a race this important.**](https://act.electjon.com/go/32?c0=ossoff-em-oct25.ZBiurg&refcode=em251009-1-f-sb&t=3&akid=895%2E5691347%2ErmjpPS) **[DONATE](https://act.electjon.com/go/32?c0=ossoff-em-oct25.ZBiurg&refcode=em251009-1-f-sb&t=4&akid=895%2E5691347%2ErmjpPS)** Thank you in advance for standing with Jon. \- JB Pritzker

name: Sen. Jeff Bridges
subject: Knock knock. The plumbers are here!
body:
The first labor union in Colorado to endorse in the Treasurer's race is backing us.

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/9d83acd1cac2/get-more-smarter-on-colorados-budget-10370136?e=b48bb2b4f4)
---
[|
---](https://bridgesforcolorado.us14.list-manage.com/track/click?u=ba078768558df9fe7d8559d49&id=fb53bc1934&e=b48bb2b4f4)
| | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | Hi there,

**Plumbers Local 3 is the first labor union in Colorado to endorse in the State Treasurer’s race, and they’re backing our campaign.**
---
|
---
| |
Plumbers Local 3 is a bedrock of skilled labor in Colorado, protecting our water, sanitation, and public health. And they don’t just do the work, they train the next generation through their Joint Apprenticeship Training Committee, keeping Colorado’s pipeline (no pun intended) of skilled tradespeople strong.
I’ve always believed that hard work should lead to good pay and a secure future. **That’s why I’ve worked to expand apprenticeships and career pathways that connect students to good-paying jobs in the skilled trades** —from plumbing to construction to clean energy.

body:
Peter,
Everywhere I travel across Colorado, one thing is clear: people are fired up.
They know what’s at stake in this election and the importance of having an Attorney General who knows how to stand up to extremists, defend our freedoms, and protect the Colorado way of life.
Coloradans are ready to elect a fighter. They want someone who will protect clean air and water, defend reproductive freedom, stand up for working families, and make sure every person and every community has a fair shot.
That’s the kind of Attorney General I will be. I’ve already shown that I will take on Trump, defend democracy, and expand access to the ballot box for every voter — Republican, Democrat, and Unaffiliated, alike. I will bring that same determination to protecting the rights and freedoms of all Coloradans as Attorney General.
This campaign isn’t just about one person. It’s about all of us — standing together, speaking out, and building a future where justice, fairness, and opportunity are not just ideals, but realities.
So let’s keep this energy going. Let’s show that when Coloradans are fired up, there’s nothing we can’t achieve. Chip in today to join our campaign and help us win this race. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/2510-q4-jg?refcode=251008-email]
Thank you,
Jena

body:
Skinny Farm Bill, ACA and No Kings ever!
| | | | |
---
| What Is In This Newsletter?

* A Seat is a Seat
* Do nothing Dan and the MAGA dream
* No Kings! October 18th
* White woman problems with ACA: Angie Girard

---
|
## A Seat Is a Seat
I've written before about my dissatisfaction for the process of electing someone to office: the endless begging for money, the shallow promises, and the duplicity of a party's support for one race over another simply because one is "high profile" while another might be in your own backyard. I'll say it again, as I always do until my throat is raw: a seat is a seat. There is not one that is worth more than another. You either control Congress, or you don't. I've even broken down the numbers before. One Senate race--say, Senator Warnock's--could have funded and flipped enough House seats to give Democrats a supermajority. But we don't do that, do we? Here in Washington's Fourth Congressional District, this seat could have been won before--and could be again this cycle--for a mere $2 million. That's less than one percent of what was spent on Warnock's race.

### The Cost of Inaction
On October 18, No Kings Day, we will likely see more people turn out to protest the 47 administration than many of us have seen in our lifetimes. People are moved by the horrors that have befallen our democracy. When a president can announce on live television that he has ended free speech and declared anti-fascism a domestic terrorist agenda, the response will be outrage and action--but it will fall short when it comes to funding elections at home. This is not a criticism of those who cannot give financially. Many people already give their time, their voice, and their courage--often at great personal sacrifice. Their commitment is what sustains democracy. But there are others among us who can do more. Those with the means to contribute must recognize that their financial support is what turns passion into progress.

### What It Takes to Win
Eighty people--that's all it takes to launch one of the most effective campaigns ever run in Congressional District 4. And just 200 people could win it. Two hundred individuals willing to raise $1.1 million, the amount needed for a viable campaign starting in February. With so much at stake--literally our lives and our freedoms--why is it so hard to find 200 people willing to commit $6,000 each? That's a small price for free speech, the right to self-governance, and protection from unwarranted search, seizure, and imprisonment. For some, that amount is out of reach, and their contributions will come in the form of volunteering, organizing, and showing up. But for others, $6,000 is entirely possible--and now is the time to give it.
### Beyond Politics as Usual
I have strong opposition to the traditional model of electoral politics and the greed that defines it. But this is different. This is a moment when a relatively small amount of money--and a great deal of heart--could truly change the course of our nation and the lives of people right here at home. We can keep waving signs, sharing social posts, and attending rallies. All of that matters deeply. But real change requires investment, in both effort and resources. It requires each of us to act with urgency and purpose, in whatever way we are able. A seat is a seat. And this one--our seat--can and should be won. The question is not whether we can afford to fight for it, but whether we can afford not to.
My crystal ball: Congressional District 8 is a lock, 3 we will keep, 4 is flippable and 5 will take more time.

---
| |
---
| Do nothing Dan and the MAGA dream
The Farm Bill is critical to the success of people in rural Washington and the nation as a whole. About eighty percent of the Farm Bill is the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP), more commonly referred to as food stamps. Congressional District 4 Representative Dan Newhouse prides himself on being one of only a handful of farmers in Congress and therefore claims to be a "significant" voice for farmers. The U.S. Congress passes the Farm Bill roughly every five years to shape national agriculture, nutrition, conservation, and forestry policy. The last time it was passed was in 2018. Newhouse was sworn in in 2015 and was already well into his second term when the Farm Bill came up for a vote.
---
---
| |
---
## From Legislating to Executive Orders

Now that we have seen a seismic shift from the Legislative Branch actually legislating to a country run by executive order, the all-important Farm Bill has been gutted by the so-called Big Beautiful Bill, H.R. 1. Along with making huge and devastating cuts to SNAP and other critical programs, it also dealt a devastating blow to Medicaid. These two cuts alone, so deep and damaging, have left rural America reeling and without a clear future. Add to this the cuts to programs such as Local Food Purchase Assistance and Local Food for Schools. Not to mention the negative impact of tariffs and cuts to foreign aid, which have reduced agricultural purchases by billions of dollars.

---
|
## SNAP Cuts and Food Insecurity

The consequences of cuts to SNAP cannot be overstated. Eighty percent of the Farm Bill is allocated to SNAP, representing billions of dollars. In Yakima County, one in five people depend on SNAP, which is twice the state average. The impact on food insecurity and the inevitable consequences that follow will rip through our community like a plague. Surprisingly, there is no MAGA spin that works here because there is no upside. Even attempts to claim protection of Americans from paying for "illegal aliens" ring too hollow for even Newhouse to mouth. Recently, [Jerry LeClaire wrote an article](https://zmhksxhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001mngDNKEhLo6aLjemOq20Bw_nH7UlzNlRaTrkwnafaTSb6XQ9hg-M4TI9tpbfSqoqg8CJ75RbqKPSyJ6UNqGHBBB5AI9-RvSDjWteqwaOFjxFIxRJmCGljk32sWStIiJS6n01-0s8EW0QvwQY4XK1yByk4dSWB-K3KHa0zqzb8afro0OvAD7Hf32pRDPcaBnXvnb0iwOxOES77GNXGxjUw1JnQQ-qyVHL&c=lh8xc7qszvPQdOKwcwPXKTtaLXEqb7mycswWrQPNZ6vfxgp1byvJ7Q==&ch=emkL_5B91AuM1JRIne9vgKWa4dB2JwsSt2eIWRQzCUjUTi5vsixcBw==) on Congressional District 5's Mike Baumgartner and his position on the Big Beautiful Bill, and it is laughable how it mirrors Newhouse. Apparently parroting MAGA talking points is preferable to actually representing one's district.

---
## [Medicaid](https://zmhksxhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001mngDNKEhLo6aLjemOq20Bw_nH7UlzNlRaTrkwnafaTSb6XQ9hg-M4TI9tpbfSqoq3aKkNvIqzclWnSXZKDJ55-d26zlJF8ZfvNrfVAENuOnDmDlnoiJ8TSZ54ntV0LNWAt86n1rodizYhCaFAi5uAxvxPs2m9HEGo_4kml46sld1cHJ4wC5xDSWgpuaTYhQFAsKrH7FKauEBqnEStbjHzRv8w4QzcMFQesqdqvYL0nyCsTTb2QOmuAuByEhPIGgn6nXl-evnP3Y=&c=lh8xc7qszvPQdOKwcwPXKTtaLXEqb7mycswWrQPNZ6vfxgp1byvJ7Q==&ch=emkL_5B91AuM1JRIne9vgKWa4dB2JwsSt2eIWRQzCUjUTi5vsixcBw==) Fallout

Cuts to Medicaid total approximately $911 billion dollars, which is just a little less than double Elon Musk's wealth. For those of us who live in rural areas, we already know how fragile and inadequate our healthcare system is. With upwards of 70 percent of the people in rural Washington dependent upon Medicaid or ACA benefits, it requires no exaggeration to describe the crushing blow to our economy and people with the loss of rural healthcare. Do Nothing Dan's white knight solution is to "fight for us" to secure our share of [$50 billion directed toward rural hospitals over the next ten years](https://zmhksxhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001mngDNKEhLo6aLjemOq20Bw_nH7UlzNlRaTrkwnafaTSb6XQ9hg-M4TI9tpbfSqoq3aKkNvIqzclWnSXZKDJ55-d26zlJF8ZfvNrfVAENuOnDmDlnoiJ8TSZ54ntV0LNWAt86n1rodizYhCaFAi5uAxvxPs2m9HEGo_4kml46sld1cHJ4wC5xDSWgpuaTYhQFAsKrH7FKauEBqnEStbjHzRv8w4QzcMFQesqdqvYL0nyCsTTb2QOmuGlEZf4x57dzA6Q-ZbVO4m0=&c=lh8xc7qszvPQdOKwcwPXKTtaLXEqb7mycswWrQPNZ6vfxgp1byvJ7Q==&ch=emkL_5B91AuM1JRIne9vgKWa4dB2JwsSt2eIWRQzCUjUTi5vsixcBw==). That amounts to just five percent of Medicaid cuts -- and it comes with huge strings attached. Even more problematic is that half of the funds are allocated based on state applications, and the other half is based on "need" as assessed at the discretion of the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS). We have already seen 47's administration's attitude toward Democratic states. What is the likelihood that this distribution will be equitable, especially with Newhouse's and 47's history?

---
|
---
## Global Market Collapse

Destroying the global market has always been a superpower of 47, and this time around is no different. During 47's first administration, his trade war with China failed so completely that he had to bail out U.S. farmers to the tune of $28 billion, the legality of which is still in question. This time his tariffs, cuts to foreign aid, gutting of local programs, and general incompetence have meant significant losses of foreign markets for U.S. farmers. China, usually one of our largest buyers of soybeans, has purchased none from the U.S. this year. Instead, they have turned to Brazil and Argentina. To add insult to injury, 47 has just promised $20 billion to Argentina. 47 has announced that he will use tariff money, because it is "pouring in," to bail out farmers. While this confirmation of failed economic policies may console some, for our farmers it is a death knell. Traditionally both price supports and bailout money have gone to select crops, excluding our fruit and vegetable growers. Again, what is the likelihood that China will want to return to the U.S. in the future -- at least not without steep and painful concessions borne by the American people.

---
## Labor Impact and Wage Suppression

Wage suppression is also on the table through reworking of the Adverse Effective Wage Rate (AEWR), which is used to calculate the wage rate for guest workers. It is set to lower the wage paid to H-2A workers. Depending on your perspective this could be good or bad, but for our communities it is bad. The AEWR was supposed to make guest workers less attractive than local labor because of the extra cost. But as farms have grown huge, it has proven far more cost-effective to pay the higher wages than to rely on local workers. Lowering H-2A wages will only make local labor even less attractive. Additionally, small farmers have largely been excluded from participating in the H-2A visa process because of the high costs and complexity. Lowering wages does not make the process more accessible to them.

---
## The MAGA Dream Fulfilled

So what does this all mean? After nearly a decade of incompetence, Dan Newhouse has accomplished the MAGA dream. He is devastating our economy, creating poverty wages, cutting healthcare, and replacing it with food insecurity -- leaving us apparently expected to be grateful for whatever crumbs are thrown our way so that a few who already have too much can have more. And now Do Nothing Dan has announced that since the Farm Bill has been gutted, he can finally pass [the "skinny" Farm Bill](https://zmhksxhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001mngDNKEhLo6aLjemOq20Bw_nH7UlzNlRaTrkwnafaTSb6XQ9hg-M4TI9tpbfSqoqchgSzTufpLfgnA011FeIcnBU6cpsUedw0-YVDzNByjG5M2b0_lrKeYgSMD1ACz1_ypOD6dWee3xU_1iEKUwrWD4AfBLcIalerIuEMwwGqOfqDb45olapFw==&c=lh8xc7qszvPQdOKwcwPXKTtaLXEqb7mycswWrQPNZ6vfxgp1byvJ7Q==&ch=emkL_5B91AuM1JRIne9vgKWa4dB2JwsSt2eIWRQzCUjUTi5vsixcBw==). My goodness.

When I read Angie Girard's most recent Substack article, I knew it was something more people needed to see. If a comfortably well-off, educated white woman can be so upended by changes to the ACA, it takes little imagination to grasp the impact on the millions of Americans who have far less security.

He then said he would “piss on his grave”. Then he went after Gilbert's family. Jones called Todd Gilbert's wife and young children "little fascists" who are "breeding" evil and should be eliminated. This isn't normal political anger, Peter. These are the fantasies of someone who clearly has problems. Any rational person who harbors these kinds of violent delusions about colleagues and their children should not seek public office. * * *
# **Breaking: Letitia James indicted on bank fraud charge**
New York Attorney General Letitia James **[was indicted by a federal grand jury in Virginia's Eastern District on a single count of bank fraud,](https://substack.com/redirect/0738fc28-0e4b-4500-8aa8-1726a26cc3f9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** following a referral from federal housing regulator Bill Pulte who alleged she "falsified records" to obtain favorable home loans for a Norfolk, Virginia property she claimed as her "principal residence" in 2023.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/b0a17a81-7d33-4078-a165-15a31a8535cc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* **Allegations of loan fraud and misrepresentation** : Pulte claimed James committed multiple offenses including wire fraud, mail fraud, and false statements to financial institutions, also alleging she misclassified her Brooklyn brownstone as having four units instead of five to potentially secure more favorable loan terms on both properties, though James has called the allegations "baseless" and said she purchased the Virginia home with her niece who lives there.
* **Political context and other charges** : Democrat NY Gov. Kathy Hochul called the indictment "weaponization of the Justice Department," occurring after James won a $355 million civil judgment against Trump's organization last year, with the FHFA head making similar mortgage fraud accusations against Sen. Adam Schiff and James Comey being indicted in the same Virginia district on September 25.

* * *
# University pushes through TPUSA chapter approval despite student gov't pushback
The University of Tennessee at Chattanooga administration **[overruled its student government's vote to block students](https://substack.com/redirect/9f7ce3eb-2a94-4af2-8218-e368c9a4d40c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** from establishing a Turning Point USA chapter, with the Dean of Students' Office determining the group is approved as a Registered Student Organization.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/9f7ce3eb-2a94-4af2-8218-e368c9a4d40c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Kirk assassination context** : The student government had voted against the chapter whose founder Charlie Kirk, 31, was shot and killed on September 10 while speaking at Utah Valley University during his "American Comeback Tour," adding emotional weight to the controversy.
* **Legal threat prompted reversal** : Trial lawyer Robert Barnes publicly threatened to sue the school on behalf of students after the initial rejection based on alleged "hate speech" concerns, receiving support from Assistant Attorney General Harmeet Dhillon, which Barnes credited as "the gamechanger" leading to approval.
* **Part of broader pattern** : The UTC decision follows recent controversies involving **[TPUSA chapters at other universities including Rutgers,](https://substack.com/redirect/27ad09eb-8bb1-44f2-b6f6-2c8befd33b3c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** where students have accused administrators and peers of political bias against conservative groups, with the university clarifying that "recognition of student organizations is determined by the UTC Dean of Students and Chancellor" regardless of student government opinions.

* * *
# **Climate activist accused of Palisades Fire arson**
Jonathan Rinderknecht, 29, a Florida man who regularly posted climate change alarmist content and anti-Trump messages on social media, **[is accused of starting the Palisades Fire on January 1 that killed 12 people,](https://substack.com/redirect/7a87edc5-491b-43ee-9663-4d0d06e86262?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** burned nearly 24,000 acres, destroyed over 7,000 structures, and caused approximately $150 billion in damages.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/7a87edc5-491b-43ee-9663-4d0d06e86262?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Ironic social media history** : Rinderknecht's Facebook page featured posts about global warming causing wildfires, climate apocalypses, pro-vegan content, and articles like "Climate Change Will Force a New American Migration" with thumbnails showing California wildfires--eerily similar to the destruction he allegedly created himself.
* **Disturbing behavior and evidence** : Prosecutors allege Rinderknecht hiked to hills above Los Angeles to start the brushfire, filmed the blaze, reported it to authorities, returned to watch firefighters battle it, created AI-generated images of burning cities, and had previously threatened to burn down his sister's house before his arrest.

While we paused, Democrats kept right on fundraising.
We should have expected nothing less from a party so radical.
| **__A Personal Note from Elise Stefanik__**
---
Friend,
As I’ve said previously, when the Democrats shut down the government at the start of the month, I paused all of our fundraising.
**The last thing I wanted to do was bother you with emails and texts at a time when millions of Americans are struggling because the Democrats decided to hold our country hostage to try and benefit _illegals_ at your expense.**
In fact, I believe so strongly that the American people need to see that _YOU_ are our ONLY priority that I’ve had my own salary withheld during the Democrats’ senseless shutdown.
_But while we were paused, the Democrats kept right on fundraising..._
| **Dems push for $15 from supporters in fundraiser, pin shutdown on Trump and GOP**
“Leading Democrats began fundraising off the government shutdown, blaming Republicans and President Donald Trump despite having **voted against a bipartisan extension** to _keep_ government operations running.”
[Source: _MEAWW News_]
---
Honestly, we should have expected nothing less from a party so radical that they were willing to shut down the government in order to give healthcare to _illegals_!
As the Democrats continued to fundraise, I realized we couldn’t remain paused and allow them to take advantage of the shutdown to gain an edge for the midterms.
...Especially not when we’re locked in two battles with razor-thin margins:
_**Right now, we’re just _1 SEAT_ over the threshold to declare a majority in the House and the latest polling shows me BEATING Kathy Hochul by _1-POINT_ once voters are made aware of our positions. **_
**But because of our pause, we’re now starting off October a week behind on fundraising.**
_Earlier this year, you helped me make up 5 months of fundraising in just a few weeks. Now, I need your help making up this week of fundraising in just a few days._
If there’s any group of grassroots Americans who can pull it off, it’s my supporters._You’ve always come through for me when I needed it most._
And now more than ever, I’m counting on your support, Friend.
We’ve fought so hard to both DEFEND the House and get into a position where, with the right messaging and support, we can BEAT Kathy Hochul and SAVE New York.
It would be devastating to squander that opportunity because we fell behind on fundraising and lacked the resources to tell Americans the TRUTH about Hochul and the Democrats.
[**So please, if you can, make a grassroots contribution to help us CATCH UP now that we’re starting off the month a week behind in fundraising – _and I’ll ensure it goes FIVE TIMES AS FAR._**](http://links.g4yamerica.com/u/click?_t=cc7dda5c2cc64061900678c88bd3a18a&_m=0055d31b7eaf4e64b7ff636e8e38180b&_e=mniOc83rwjRKpYUjTg2as1JhHPp8Ckf1obLeTowisgj3-kCyPpIFcnUlyguNjEkPV1mA15Pilcmvm4QQWt7VuH2ddd_gKSteLhzLRfaM9Z1Ba7nRcCnxfKXq48-9XFU6TrU2gHQTwwS2gnrP7NxTFpL9R9Zsz6I9qWfWDGtj5od5JX_BLNcbBIZk25XOkgxdoWciX_rnSADqLqhInLfIimn7FzYwBNyyRWats2Mq3efD-fLHePLIzN1-aHzmnS3651YkHvSUWLnVzPynexnLy_8gRDe5f68KuoqCoY7dPhP-A4asa25NVxEP6e8H7vFgs8mnRc1v78gvjtVf3XA8x_vRB-_7MDqv5ginq_a9kQ5aLRGR0_v42ZKGECmVovCn9C2DrOjvHkL9hh1CB2fzLV7vncyU7RRawqAb2qb1AmSoMw94rvyiBu4BbZ02utrcamFiTHJZ4ZpTvxpMSv2BURy2JvkUHKGFFCyl7WWJucFtbds6VmRTf7YnFietw7WZc2-Xs_kEtV60Uq9VUgrVSS2_j3mBm09qLb9QUE5fD40dCcBh3o654BIST15uK8LsqXnQ3xagXbLjQ8gWz6ASuPVl3fKGhrpqi0AYcxErT5c%3D)

[ ](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/116949197/574966643/1435897075?refcode=email_100925_numbers&refcode2=sl2&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS83MjY1OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI1ZGMzYjZmZi01ZGE1LWYwMTEtOGU2MS02MDQ1YmRlZDhiYTQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=tzccsW3rFFA3TRprn0B8fUepRYbGjtBVZ88cYgXc1_M=&emci=4bc3b6ff-5da5-f011-8e61-6045bded8ba4&emdi=5dc3b6ff-5da5-f011-8e61-6045bded8ba4&ceid=7280715) We know we’ve been messaging you a lot about John Hickenlooper’s must-win race in Colorado, but we wanted to share some numbers that will put things into perspective: **$48 MILLION.** That’s the amount that Republicans spent trying to defeat John Hickenlooper in 2020. **$600 MILLION.** That’s how much Donald Trump has vowed to spend in the midterms next year to expand the Republican Senate majority and keep a tight grip on his power in Washington. **$27.31.** That was John Hickenlooper’s average online contribution last month. Welcome friends!
We went live with a hell of an "Amped Up" show this week. [David Shuster](https://open.substack.com/users/16891317-david-shuster?utm_source=mentions) and I dove straight into the chaos -- from the overdue Netanyahu/Hamas ceasefire to Trump's economic demolition derby.
We then brought in one of the sharpest minds out there to make sense of it all: [Marlon Weems](https://open.substack.com/users/158194-marlon-weems?utm_source=mentions), founder of the first Black-owned financial services firm in Arkansas and one of the clearest, most principled economic voices in America today.
Marlon doesn't mince words. He's got the kind of insight that comes from decades on the inside of Wall Street's machine, watching exactly how the gears of money, power, and politics grind ordinary people to dust.
He's also got something that can be challenging to find in that world: _a conscience_.
We started with the global circus. Israel and Hamas had just announced a ceasefire, one Netanyahu could have had a year ago if he hadn't been busy flexing his authoritarian muscles (this is meant in no way to exonerate the ghouls of Hamas, btw).
As David put it, the deal only happened because Trump's crew outmaneuvered Netanyahu after his reckless strike on Qatar.
And you know what? As much as it pains me, we gave them credit--[though let's be honest, Trump himself had no idea what was going on](https://substack.com/redirect/b79ff1d1-88b1-46f2-8e64-8da64997ebe7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Someone in his orbit must've made a rational decision while he was cheating at golf or trying on one of his extra-super-big-but-not-that-tall suits.
But as I said on air, we'll give credit when it's earned, even to people we despise.

Then we pivoted to America's slow-motion economic arson, a perfect segue to bring in Marlon.
Because if you want to understand how [Trump and his little henchmen are dismantling both democracy ](https://substack.com/redirect/2ffcd1a8-0472-4300-8be8-d58854a56ac8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_[and](https://substack.com/redirect/2ffcd1a8-0472-4300-8be8-d58854a56ac8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_[ the economy](https://substack.com/redirect/2ffcd1a8-0472-4300-8be8-d58854a56ac8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), who better than someone who explores how money, markets, and politics intersect--and how those forces shape the lives of everyday people.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/1c173266-1474-4690-a711-571a0ca99536?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Marlon didn't hesitate.
He said what most TV pundits are too timid or bought-off to say: _Trump 's economic plan is chaos by design._ Global tariffs that tanked U.S. farmers, deportations that wiped out entire sectors of the labor force, debt explosions that hollowed out the dollar.
[It's all self-sabotage, like sending troops into our own cities.](https://substack.com/redirect/327b5c58-2b8c-4349-b418-17ba6f9ed4e4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Or, as Marlon put it so perfectly:
> These guys aren't idiots. They know exactly what they're doing. They're creating crisis so they can profit off the cleanup.
It's disaster capitalism, MAGA-style, and it's frightening how much it parallels what Putin did early on to consolidate power in Russia.
You wreck the economy, you drive the middle class into a panic, and while everyone's too busy worrying about rent and health insurance, your billionaire pals swoop in to buy pieces of the country wholesale.
When I laid out all the pieces: tariffs, deportations, government shutdowns, credit downgrades, the hollowing out of the Bureau of Labor Statistics, Marlon connected the dots. The result?
A populace paralyzed by uncertainty. Nobody knows what comes next.
You can't plan, can't save, can't even buy a damn car without wondering if the government will implode before your first payment clears. And that uncertainty isn't accidental; _it 's authoritarianism 101_.
Keep people scared, exhausted, and too busy surviving to fight back. [But fight back ](https://substack.com/redirect/217bd260-5727-46df-a7ec-feb3ae577a70?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[we must.](https://substack.com/redirect/217bd260-5727-46df-a7ec-feb3ae577a70?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

* * *
Then we talked bubbles. Housing. Crypto. The stock market.
Marlon broke down why the "booming" markets we keep hearing about are a mirage -- inflated by tax code manipulation, corporate buybacks, and the so-called "Magnificent Seven" tech monopolies that distort every index. As he said:
> You can't have gold and stocks both soaring at the same time. Those are opposite signals. Something's about to blow.
And if that wasn't sobering enough, David reminded us that Trump's crew is now folding unstable crypto holdings into people's asset evaluations for home loans. It's the same delusional math that crashed the economy in 2008.
But with fewer rules, more fraud and worse people in charge (and who thought that was possible??).
Marlon and I both tried to figure out what gives Bitcoin legitimate value, and we came up empty. My theory? "Give me a couple chickens over Bitcoin any day. At least chickens lay eggs so the brunches will be good." The only thing less valuable?
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/d656d3e1-7f1e-40cc-b2cb-315ffcd1f1bb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
On the bright side, though, you're compelled to hurl if you look at it early in the morning, so you'll keep your weight down.
We kept circling back to the same theme, the widening wealth gap and what happens when the billionaire class pulling up the life rafts from their yachts as everyone else drowns.
Marlon told us about a Citigroup report he'd seen years ago. A grotesque little memo teaching their richest clients how to _profit from inequality_.
Am I the only one who reads this and thinks it's about time to start making movies like _The Parallax View_ , _Network_ and _The China Syndrome_ again? Maybe it'd make few more people will think about the surreal, insane world in which we're currently living.
As Marlon made clear, they only have one worry, that "the masses might eventually realize the game is rigged." That's the whole damn system right there in one sentence.
And I think not only do a lot of us already realize this, whether you're impoverished, working class, middle class or upper middle class, but more of us are acting on the knowledge that the billionaires are robbing all of us via their middle men--Trump and other MAGAs.

* * *
As David pointed out, two-thirds of Americans now say the American Dream is dead. People are [working two jobs, drowning in student debt, and watching the same billionaires who caused it all lecture them about "hard work."](https://substack.com/redirect/1c173266-1474-4690-a711-571a0ca99536?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Combine that hopelessness with two guns for every person in this country and a tsunami of online disinformation, and you've got a recipe for a real American crisis.
Marlon agreed.
He said it feels like we're "repealing the last half of the 20th century," undoing every bit of progress from the New Deal to civil rights to The Great Society.
And, yes, middle class that made this country strong--the largest middle class in the history of the world--is being erased. Like they're Trump's name in the Epstein files with 1000 FBI officers working on redactions.
That's when I said straight out what I've been saying a lot lately: this is our _FDR moment_. Either we rebuild institutions and create who new ones that actually serve the people, or we watch the fascists fill the void with demagoguery.
And damn if Marlon didn't deliver the perfect closing shot.
> Forget trying to win over Republicans. Go get the 250 million people who didn't vote. That's where democracy lives.
That's the line that stuck with me. That's the fight we've got ahead. Sure, I'm happy to bring some disaffected Republicans--and there are many of them--along for the ride. But that's not our target audience.
Before signing off, we made sure everyone knew where to find Marlon: **The Journeyman on Substack** : _[thejourneyman.substack.com](https://substack.com/redirect/2a82a06f-b7d6-4e63-a95f-7f98e228fdd8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_.

Marlon Weems is one of the good ones.
A brilliant analyst, a truth-teller, and, as David said, just a genuinely good guy. Conversations like this remind me why we do _Amped Up_ in the first place: to shine a bright light through the fog, to connect the dots corporate media won't touch.
[To fight like hell for a future that still belongs to ](https://substack.com/redirect/1c173266-1474-4690-a711-571a0ca99536?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[all of us](https://substack.com/redirect/1c173266-1474-4690-a711-571a0ca99536?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[.](https://substack.com/redirect/1c173266-1474-4690-a711-571a0ca99536?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Because the stakes aren't theoretical anymore. They're our jobs, our rights, our democracy. And if we don't fight smart, fight hard, and fight _together_ , we'll lose it all to the billionaires and their hired bullies.

We then brought in one of the sharpest minds out there to make sense of it all: , founder of the first Black-owned financial services firm in Arkansas and one of the clearest, most principled economic voices in America today. He's also got something that can be challenging to find in that world: a conscience. We started with the global circus.
