body:
[1]Justice Democrats

Peter,

We just endorsed State Rep. Justin J. Pearson for Congress in Tennessee —
and the first 24 hours have been incredible.

People across Memphis, Tennessee, and the rest of the country are fed up
with the Democratic Party’s failure to stand up for the working class and
fight back against billionaires like Trump and Musk.

The first days of a campaign are mission-critical,
Peter. If we don’t raise the
early resources Justin needs now, then we won’t be able to take on Rep.
Steve Cohen — a deeply entrenched incumbent with millions of his own
personal wealth who’s coasted in this seat for nearly two decades — and
win in next August’s Democratic primary.

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20251009-jp.e1ufL2&refcode=em20251009-37092&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1002&akid=37092%2E1203867%2ERnFigJ ]Can you split a donation of whatever you can today to keep up the
momentum for Justin’s people-powered campaign?

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20251009-jp.e1ufL2&refcode=em20251009-37092&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1003&akid=37092%2E1203867%2ERnFigJ ]Split $5

This race isn’t simply about one Democrat versus another: it’s about our
movement to give power back to the working class and stop our nation’s
rapid slide into fascism.

We’re talking about a working-class champion running to represent the
working-class community he was born and raised in, going up against a
status quo career politician who has far less energy and far less focus on
the people of District 9.

It embodies the struggles everyday people are facing across this country
right now, as billionaires like Donald Trump and Elon Musk stage a
corporate coup, robbing everyday people of their right to live in a clean
environment, their jobs and fair wages, their personal data, their earned
benefits like Social Security, Medicare, and Medicaid, and their most
fundamental rights — all to lower taxes for their billionaire friends and
line their own pockets.

Cohen is an out-of-touch, absentee politician who believes he doesn’t have
to engage his community because this seat belongs to him, not the everyday
people whose struggles he’s ignored for decades. Musk and Trump are on the
same side of this fight, using their money to stay in power at the expense
of the communities they’re tasked to represent. To fight back against this
administration’s fascism, we need fighters for the working class in
Washington — not more of the 1% in Congress.

Justin is running to be that fearless voice for the working class. He
knows that this moment demands new, progressive leaders with lived
experience who will fight with the boldness and urgency our crises deserve
— not more do-nothing Democrats who stay silent while Trump and the
billionaires run rampant.

If we’re going to win the biggest fights, we need the biggest coalition
possible in Congress. Justin would join our progressive bloc of proven
champions as another critical voice and vote on the most pressing issues
of our time.

Peter, what
happens next is so important. We can either help Justin get his campaign

name: David Hogg
subject: Why I left the DNC — and what we’re building instead
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY LEADERS WE DESERVE, LEADERSWEDESERVE
body:
The change Democrats need starts with these candidates.
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20251009-1&t=1&akid=2730%2E587540%2E9cATfe)
Hi Peter,
We just rolled out our latest round of 2026 endorsements — and I couldn't be prouder or more excited about these candidates.
**Peter, this is _exactly_ why I left the DNC.** Too many Democrats in D.C. are silent, complacent, and beholden to special interests. They treat public office like something they’re _owed_ — not a responsibility to earn from the people they serve.
At Leaders We Deserve, we’re building a new generation of young, progressive leaders — an inspiring vision for the Democratic Party that people _actually like and want to vote for._
Take **Justin Pearson** — a bold, effective leader who always does what’s right for his community — not for his own political safety. One of the **“Tennessee Three,”** Republicans expelled Justin from the state legislature for standing up to the NRA after a school shooting. He also stopped a billion-dollar corporation from building a harmful oil pipeline in his community.
Now, he’s challenging a longtime Congressman in Tennessee’s 9th District who has failed to deliver for Memphis — and we couldn’t be more excited to back him.
Then there’s **Donavan McKinney** in Michigan’s 13th District. Donovan’s challenging one of the most corrupt and ineffective Democrats in D.C — a guy who takes millions from AIPAC, broke his no-corporate-PAC pledge, and spent more taxpayer money on advertising than any other member of Congress.
Donovan’s the opposite — he delivers real results for Detroit, including millions for gun violence prevention, replacing lead pipes, and taking on private utilities that have long controlled Michigan politics.
Our other endorsees share their courage:
* **Christian Menefee (TX-18)** — As Houston’s County Attorney, he’s proven he’s not afraid to take on the powerful — including Trump, mega-polluters, and corporate fraudsters.
* **Randy Villegas (CA-22)** — An educator, organizer, and proud son of immigrants who can flip a highly competitive swing seat — but first must win a primary against one of California’s most conservative Democrats.
* **Akbar Ali (GA-HD-106)** — At **21 years old,** he would be the youngest state rep in Georgia history (after LWD-backed Bryce Berry) — proving young people can beat the odds to lead with courage.

This is what real leadership looks like — and it’s why I walked away from the DNC.
Leaders We Deserve is building the next generation of bold, progressive leaders who put people and doing what’s right over winning a re-election campaign.
But they can’t win without you, Peter. Our candidates don’t take a dime of corporate PAC money — they’re counting on grassroots supporters like you to win tough races and defeat entrenched incumbents bankrolled by special interests.
**[Will you pitch in $5 to help us build a new generation of bold, progressive leaders?](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20251009_1_endorse.ZV_YZP&refcode=em20251009-2730&amount=5&t=3&akid=2730%2E587540%2E9cATfe)**
**[Donate $5 »](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20251009_1_endorse.ZV_YZP&amount=5&refcode=em20251009-2730&t=22&akid=2730%2E587540%2E9cATfe)**
I’m so proud and excited about the work we’re doing and what’s ahead — and I’m so grateful that you’re a part of it.
Thank you,
David Hogg

Peter,

As the government shutdown drags on, the White House is pushing an unprecedented assault on NASA and America’s leadership in science.

**The Trump Administration has proposed a 25% cut to NASA and would cancel half the agency’s science efforts – the largest-scale attack on the agency in its history.**

I’m not allowing this to fly under the radar. I was proud to serve NASA as Chief of Staff under President Obama. In my time there, we put aside petty politics for the good of our position in space and science – moving the country forward, united in our mission.

**[We must save NASA and continue investing in innovation, discovery, and our country’s future in space. name: Gavin Newsom
subject: Quick update on the 9 months since the Palisades and Eaton Fires that tore through Los Angeles
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Yes on 50, The Election Rigging Response Act, Governor Newsom’s Ballot Measure Committee
body:
We've asked for federal disaster aid for months now and President Trump has said nothing.

I wanted to take a quick break from the Prop 50 emails to give an update on the Palisades and Eaton Fires that tore through Los Angeles.
It's been over 9 months now. We've asked for federal disaster aid for months now and President Trump has said nothing. The Speaker of the House has said he’s not interested in helping the American people.
I was proud to have Speaker Johnson’s back when his district was devastated. I said the same thing to Governor Abbott as we sent him personnel in support -- because he needed it, given the devastation of the flood.
I find it shameful that they haven't done a damn thing for the thousands of people who lost their homes and whose lives were devastated by this disaster in California.
**[Please watch this short video on the topic.](https://act.gavinnewsom.com/go/5170?t=1&akid=2660%2E4767699%2E74B4sg)**
[](https://act.gavinnewsom.com/go/5170?t=2&akid=2660%2E4767699%2E74B4sg)
They are abandoning Americans while building ballrooms and decorating Trump's office gold. It's disgusting and disqualifying.
Gavin Newsom
* * *
i️ To my fellow Democrats — don't scroll past this. 🇺🇸
I have heard the calls do "Do something!" and I agree. If Texas wants to redraw their maps, California will fight fire with fire.
God help us if we're not successful. We may have enjoyed our last free and fair election. They're redrawing districts to hold the House; going after ActBlue and Democrats' ability to fundraise; going after colleges and the free press... We have to act.

name: Heidi Ganahl
subject: The Mountain Minute: 10/9/2025
body:
Inside the $361 million standoff over Colorado’s unfunded mandates
| | | | [](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
---
**PRESENTED BY[ROCKYMOUNTAINVOICE.COM](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
| | Hi friends,
Here is a summary of today's top stories:
🏔️ **Here in Colorado...** Governor Jared Polis is touting city compliance with new housing mandates even as six municipalities—including Aurora and Greenwood Village—sue the state, calling the rules [unconstitutional under home-rule protections](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.). In La Plata County, co-op members are [suing over a $210 million Tri-State exit](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) approved without a member vote, and the Colorado Supreme Court expanded who can [sue over secret government meetings](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), boosting transparency.
Meanwhile, Logan County families face [foreclosure amid a failed water system](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), and a new lawsuit accuses Polis’s administration of [enabling “forced labor” in state prisons](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.). Denver is [cutting 311 hours](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) and turning to AI amid budget shortfalls, while a [$361 million dispute over unfunded mandates](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) pits local governments against the state.
**🇺🇸 On the National Stage...** Washington and the courts are roiled by revelations and rebukes. A Lancet-published NIH study buried findings showing [vaccinated children faced higher risks of long COVID](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) and organ issues, reigniting debate over research transparency. At the Supreme Court, Justice Samuel Alito [blasted Colorado for “blatant viewpoint discrimination”](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) in Chiles v. Salazar. And AG Pam Bondi clashed with Senate Democrats in a [fiery Judiciary hearing](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), calling out partisan hypocrisy.
🗣️ **Commentary Spotlight...** Denver business owner Michael Whitcomb urges voters to reject the $950 million “Vibrant Denver” bond, warning it [would worsen the city’s $250 million deficit](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.). He argues leaders are disguising tax impacts while borrowing billions for redundant projects, calling for fiscal discipline over more debt as Denver’s population and business base decline.
This is the Mountain Minute for Thursday, October 9, 2025.
– Team RMV
---
|
---
**TODAY'S TOP STORIES**
**[Fix It or Fund It: Inside the $361 million standoff over Colorado’s unfunded mandates](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY JEN SCHUMANN, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
Mesa County Commissioner Bobbie Daniel didn’t set out to launch a statewide revolt. Two years ago, she created a spreadsheet to track state mandates that came without funding. The goal was to help department heads navigate budgeting headaches. But that quiet act of accounting has since grown into something far louder—a bipartisan movement spanning more than 36 counties, with local governments now invoking state law to declare state mandates “optional.”
“We started this whole unfunded mandate tracker... trying to see how I could better serve my constituents,” Daniel explained during a Sept. 29 commission meeting. “But also my department heads, who are having to deal with the significant effects of an unfunded mandate yearly.”
Mesa County alone has estimated more than $10 million annually in costs related to unfunded mandates. If similar burdens are carried by Colorado’s other 63 counties, the statewide impact could exceed $361 million per year.
**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|
---
**[Some thoughts worth considering before city folk vote on the “Vibrant Denver” bond](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY MICHAEL WHITCOMB, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
* Denver business owner Michael Whitcomb warns that the proposed $950 million “Vibrant Denver” bond would worsen the city’s $250 million deficit and reward poor fiscal management.

* He argues that projects like new parks, housing, and cultural funding duplicate existing programs and hide real costs behind misleading claims that taxes won’t rise.

* Whitcomb urges voters to reject ballot issues 2A–2E, saying Denver must focus on financial discipline and service delivery rather than taking on more debt as population and business revenue decline.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|
---
The Rocky Mountain Voice is a 501(c)(3) that exists to promote informed civic engagement and the principles of self-governance through enterprise reporting on public policy, politics, government, and culture throughout the state of Colorado. The only way we can continue to spread truth is with your support!
[DONATE TO ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
|
---
**[When the prosecutor is also the judge: Colorado’s due process problem under Griswold’s watch](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY CORY GAINES, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
* The commentary by Cory Gaines exposes alleged bias and due process violations within Colorado’s administrative hearings, particularly under Secretary of State Jena Griswold’s office.

* Gaines highlights a case where Griswold’s office tripled a fine against the conservative “No on EE” campaign—after its own hearing officer imposed a lower penalty—demonstrating how prosecutors and judges effectively operate under the same authority.

* He warns that this system allows unelected officials to act as both enforcers and arbiters, undermining the separation of powers and eroding public trust in fair, impartial governance.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|

**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)****[Is Rep. Marshall’s narrow 2024 win now at risk in Douglas County?](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)****BY SHAINA COLE | COMMENTARY | OCTOBER 7** _Rep. Bob Marshall (D-HD43) represents one of Colorado’s most politically mixed suburban districts, covering parts of Highlands Ranch and Littleton. The area is built around families, good schools, and a long-standing belief in local control and fiscal restraint._
____
**[Colorado: Where Criminals Come to Stay and Play](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** **BY MIKE O'DONNELL | COMMENTARY | OCTOBER 6** _The FBI recently released detailed data on more than 14 million criminal offenses from calendar year 2024, reported to the Uniform Crime Reporting (UCR) Program by participating law enforcement agencies. More than 16,000 state, county, city, university, college, and tribal agencies, covering around 95.6% of the population of the United States, submitted data to the UCR Program through the National Incident-Based Reporting System and the Summary Reporting System._
**[“This is too important to improvise”: D49 superintendent says sports lawsuit seeks clarity](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**BY JEN SCHUMANN | LOCAL | OCTOBER 6** _Colorado Springs’ School District 49 made headlines in May when it filed a federal lawsuit challenging the state’s anti-discrimination law and CHSAA’s transgender athlete policy. “We wanted to get in front of the coming legal conflict,” he explained in an interview with RMV. “We think this is too important to improvise.”_ **[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**__

**✈️ DID YOU KNOW?** **The first commercial passenger flight lasted just 23 minutes.** In 1914, former St. Petersburg mayor Abram Pheil made history when he paid $400—about $12,600 today—for a 23-minute flight across Tampa Bay. The short trip, piloted by Tony Jannus, covered just 21 miles between St. Petersburg and Tampa. Though brief, that flight marked the dawn of commercial air travel and set the stage for the global aviation industry we know today.
